summary: gs-rest-service release: dynamic glibc (as built now) against fully static musl (flint package), runtime on the Spring workload and stripped O3/Oz against Go; non-gating
why: Go's comparator is fully static. Flint's glibc release build maps about 1.75 MB of shared-library text (gc.md 1.4). Fully static under ADR-023 means the musl target. Allocator confound, recorded as the coordinator asked: musl's mallocng replaces glibc malloc for the native libraries (openssl, llhttp, libpq) and for druntime's own pools. So this compares what a musl-static Flint app would really run on in production, not linking alone; an extra arm with mallocng in the dynamic build may separate it if that is cheap. Decision rule: the measured release profile switches to static only if Oz still passes against Go and no runtime metric gets worse beyond its interval; size and runtime then use the same static build, with the dynamic series as context. Method (tools/spring_static_ab.py): both binaries pass 18/18 exact first; the manifest's phases unchanged; 6 runs per arm, the arms alternating (about 27 minutes); Go is not loaded in this window (its runtime numbers come from the gs-rest-multicore runs). Each metric is reported as the ratio of medians (static / dynamic) with a bootstrap 99% interval.

argv: {"dynamic-glibc": {"build": ["flint", "build", "--profile", "release"], "binary": ".flint/build/release/gs-rest-service", "Oz": {"build": ["flint", "build", "--profile", "size"], "binary": ".flint/build/size/gs-rest-service"}}, "static-musl": {"build": ["flint", "package", "--target", "linux-x86_64-musl"], "binary": ".flint/build/release/gs-rest-service", "Oz": {"build": null, "binary": null, "note": "TBD: m7-flint-cli's static Oz option"}}}
